answer_raw:
Anthropic's latest models are **Claude Fable 5.2** and **Claude Mythos 5.2** (as of 11-09-2026) [3], while OpenAI's latest is the **GPT-6** family, specifically **GPT-6.1 Terra** (as of 10-26-2026) and the **Astra** model (as of 09-04-2026) [1][5].

## Model Comparison

The competition between these two ecosystems currently centers on a trade-off between specialized technical capability and broad operational utility.

**Anthropic's lineup** — The Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models (as of 11-09-2026) are designed for "daunting technical work," offering 30% faster outputs than previous versions and improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision [3]. While Fable 5.2 is broadly available, Mythos 5.2 is restricted to organizations in Anthropic's Life Sciences and Cyber verification programs [3].

**OpenAI's lineup** — The GPT-6 **Astra** model (asty 09-04-2026) is positioned as a state-of-the-art model for software engineering, cyber security, and "computer use," with claims from leadership that it represents artificial general intelligence (AGI) [5]. For high-scale deployment, **GPT-6.1 Terra** (as of 10-26-2026) focuses on fast, capable computer use at scale [1]. 

## Coding Verdict

If you are looking for a specialized technical tool, I would use **Claude Fable 5.2** (as of 11-09-2026). Anthropic has built its models to handle complex technical tasks, and the Fable 5.2 release specifically targets coding and reasoning improvements [3].

However, if your coding workflow involves heavy agentic automation or "computer use" (where the AI interacts with your desktop or browser), **GPT-6 Astra** (as of 09-04-2026) is the stronger candidate. It is specifically marketed as being state-of-the-art for software engineering and professional work [5].
